name: Base64 and Hex
tagline: Text to bytes to Base64, hex, percent or binary.
description:
Five encodings over the same path: the text is turned into UTF-8 bytes first, then written as Base64, URL-safe Base64, spaced hex, percent encoding or bits. Decoding runs the same path backwards and validates strictly, so a truncated Base64 string or an odd-length hex string is reported rather than silently padded into nonsense.

Hex input tolerates the shapes hex is usually pasted in — spaces, colons, commas and 0x prefixes are ignored. URL-safe Base64 is re-padded before decoding. Decoded bytes that are not valid UTF-8 raise an error instead of producing replacement characters.

The byte count under the output is the count of the bytes, not of the characters, which is the number that matters when something has a limit. "Move output to input" flips the direction and feeds the result back, so a round trip is one click.
releaseNotes: Added a binary mode and strict UTF-8 decoding. Hex input now accepts 0x prefixes and colon separators.
